_comment: The workspace failure the 2026-09-29 root run explained, thanks to the conjuncts being recorded.
Seven of eight parts passed. The workspace was made, its path was announced, EXIT said it was
removed and the host agreed it was gone. Only 'the tool wrote in it' failed - because the command
was `pwd; touch made-here && echo WROTE_WORKSPACE; ls -ld .` while the lease allow-listed /bin/sh
and nothing else. touch and ls are separate binaries, so the kernel refused both, correctly, and
the check read that as the daemon failing to provide a usable workspace.
The test was asking for execs it had not declared. Check 16 already had the discipline - 'All from
sh builtins, so each lease needs nothing but /bin/sh' - and check 17 did not follow it. The command
is now `pwd; : > made-here && echo WROTE_WORKSPACE`, which creates the file with a redirection and
This fixture holds the OLD shape, so the composite must be false while the conjuncts name the cause:
created true, announced true, exit-says-removed true, gone-from-host true, wrote-in-it FALSE. Before
the conjuncts were recorded, all of that was a single False and diagnosing it needed another root run.
